title: Citation-integrity net only recognises a bare '[n]' marker; a bracketed group '[2, 3]' or a prose pseudo-citation '[New findings]' ships as literal, unresolved text in the published brief
repro: Round-2 gate re-drive, candidate 4c6dfe8c2d939ce3557e977a3ddcf802931ac2a2, own sidecar 127.0.0.1:52321 (data dir scratchpad/rc1-data-rc1-drive-research-briefs-r2). (a) BDL DEEP, openai gpt-4o-mini (docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/rc1/r2/1-deep-bdl-4omini.stdout.txt): published markdown contains four literal '[New findings]' tokens ('an operating margin of 10.98% [New findings]', 'increase by approximately 5.47% year-over-year [New findings]', 'Order Book: ... [New findings]', 'Dividend per Share: ₹4.90 [New findings]') that resolve to nothing on the numbered source rail. (b) Kaynes ULTRA, openai gpt-4o-mini, heavy mode (.../3-ultra-kaynes-4omini.stdout.txt): published markdown contains bracketed multi-citation groups '[2, 3]' and '[2, 4]'. Direct repro: python3 -c "import re; print(re.compile(r'\[(\d{1,3})\](?!\()').findall('[2, 3]'))" -> [] (no match at all) on both sidecar/services/research/citecheck.py's MARKER_RE and src/lib/brief-ingest.ts's CITE_MARKER_RE (identical pattern, digits-only, no comma/prose allowed). Because the pattern requires the bracket to contain ONLY 1-3 digits, neither '[New findings]' nor '[2, 3]' is ever matched -- so strip_invalid_markers() (citecheck.py) never evaluates them as out-of-range, strip_model_bibliography()'s _N_LITERAL_RE only catches the literal string '[n]' (not other bracketed prose), and brief-ingest.ts never turns them into a resolvable citation chip either. Both patterns ship through verbatim as dead bracket text in front of the user, undermining the citation-integrity guarantee the R8/citecheck system exists to provide (R15-RESEARCH-029's fix_shape explicitly aimed for 'reject or rewrite [n]-literal markers'; this is the same defect class -- the net only covers the exact string '[n]' and a bare integer, not the wider space of bracketed non-numeric or multi-numeric tokens a model naturally writes).
